punchline: During REM sleep, the brain's stress chemical noradrenaline shuts off completely, the only time in the whole day that happens.
thirty_sec: Matthew Walker showed people upsetting images in a brain scanner, then showed them again twelve hours later. People who slept in between reacted far less, and their amygdala calmed down; people who stayed awake didn't. Walker credits REM sleep, when the stress chemical noradrenaline is switched off, letting the brain keep the memory but drop the sting.
